p:cNvPr.descr: A two-part diagram illustrating SOS response in E. coli. Starting at the top is an oval blue track that is interspersed with different color segments, each one with a short red end. Starting at the bottom center of the track is a white opening outlined in blue. Inside of the opening are tan lines that outline the inside of the opening, except rather than going all around, the line stops at the top middle part. This opening area is labeled 1, which reads, “Damage to DNA produces single-strand gap.” To the left of this is the blue, followed by a peach segment, labeled lexA. An arrow points up from lexA to a peach ball, labeled LexA repressor. Simultaneously, a red arrow points from the balls to the red segment at the end of the peach segment. The red arrow is connected to a red curved line that travels the diameter of the inside of the track. To the left of the peach segment is another blue, followed by a yellow segment labeled dinF, attached to a peach ball on the inside near its red end, followed by the blue, then a gray segment labeled uvrA, followed by the blue, then a light green segment labeled polB, followed by the blue, then a tan section labeled dinB, followed by the blue, then a brown section labeled uvrB, followed by the blue, then an orange section labeled sulA, followed by the blue, then a purple section labeled umuC,D, followed by the blue, then a green section labeled recA, followed by another blue that is right of the opening previously described. All of the colored sections, except the blue, have red segments at the right end where peach balls are attached. The red line that travels all around the inside of the structure has short curved arrows pointing from it to the peach balls around. Where recA is located, a dashed arrow points away from the green segment and up to a small, green spherical structure labeled RecA protein. There are three additional spheres on the inside of the structure. The blue track structure in its entirety is labeled E. coli chromosome. Beneath the entire structure is the text, “Replication,” which has short dashed arrows to its left and right, and an arrow pointing down to a similar structure as just described. This time, however, the opening at the bottom is much wider, and where the tan line stops, there are a series of five green spherical balls slotted into the space. This is labeled 2, which states, “RecA binds to single-stranded DNA.” To the right of these spheres is a series of nine other green spheres, with a curved yellow arrow pointing up at them; this is labeled activated proteolysis. An arrow curves up and left to five peach balls (which have been pushed away from the red segments of the colored sections, except for the one on lexA). The peach balls are cracked in half, showing a white space across the middle of each one. This is labeled 3, and states, “LexA repressor is inactivated.” Each of the small red arrows that were pointing to the peach balls have now disappeared, along with the red line that spanned the entire inside of the structure. Now there are small curved arrows (all black) pointing directly from the colored segments to small boulders of the same color; dinF points to 2 yellow; uvrA points to 1 gray, polB points to 1 light green; dinB points to 3 tan; uvrB points to 2 brown; sulA points to 1 orange, and umuC,D points to 1 purple.
